sentences.en: U-R-S-P-R-A-C-H-E, or Straha Kavadis.
sentences.zh: U-R-S-P-R-A-C-H-E，或者说 Urspräche。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that effort matters.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道努力很重要。

sentences.en: What was revelatory to me was how much it mattered.
sentences.zh: 但让我感到醍醐灌顶的是，努力竟然如此重要。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: What is it that makes extraordinary people successful?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么让杰出人物获得成功？

sentences.en: Is it talent?
sentences.zh: 是天赋吗？

sentences.en: Genius?
sentences.zh: 是天才吗？

sentences.en: Luck?
sentences.zh: 是运气吗？

sentences.en: Or as Angela Duckworth suggests, is it grit?
sentences.zh: 还是像安吉拉·达克沃斯（Angela Duckworth）所说的那样，是坚毅（grit）？

sentences.en: There is a fluency and an ease with which true mastery and expertise always expresses itself,
sentences.zh: 真正的精通和专业知识在展现时，总是带着一种流畅与从容，

sentences.en: whether it be in writing, whether it be in a mathematical proof.
sentences.zh: 无论是在写作中，还是在数学证明中。

sentences.en: But I think the question is, where does that fluency and mastery come from?
sentences.zh: 但我认为问题在于，这种流畅与精通究竟从何而来？

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, we explore this quality that Angela says is responsible for so much excellence and achievement.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将探讨安吉拉所说的这种造就了卓越与成就的品质。

sentences.en: And then we ask, does grit also have a downside?
sentences.zh: 随后我们要问，坚毅是否也有其阴暗面？

sentences.en: Sometimes people with high grit might not do the logical, rational thing because their grit compels them to keep going.
sentences.zh: 有时，坚毅程度高的人可能不会做出合乎逻辑、理性的选择，因为他们的坚毅迫使他们必须坚持到底。

sentences.en: Angela Duckworth is a psychology professor at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 安吉拉·达克沃斯是宾夕法尼亚大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: She first became interested in grit while working as a math teacher for middle school and high school students.
sentences.zh: 她在担任中学老师时，第一次对“坚毅”产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: Angela told me that when she started teaching, she noticed right away which kids were the quickest learners,
sentences.zh: 安吉拉告诉我，她刚开始教书时，立刻就注意到哪些孩子学得最快，

sentences.en: the most naturally talented, you might say.
sentences.zh: 或者说，哪些孩子最有天赋。

sentences.en: These were the kids who, when she explained the concept once, were immediately raising their hands to answer questions.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子在听她讲解一遍概念后，就会立刻举手回答问题。

sentences.en: You know, I immediately thought to myself as a young and, you know, wrong teacher that,
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一个年轻且（你知道的）经验不足的老师，我当时立刻心想：

sentences.en: OK, those are the kids by the end of the year are going to have progressed the fartheSt.
sentences.zh: “好吧，这些孩子到年底肯定会进步最大。”

sentences.en: Because I had other kids for whom it's like I put up the first problem, I show it to them,
sentences.zh: 因为我还有其他一些孩子，我给他们出第一道题，给他们演示一遍，

sentences.en: I put up the second problem, I show them a different way, I sit down with them,
sentences.zh: 我出第二道题，换种方法给他们演示，我坐下来陪着他们，

sentences.en: and OK, the fourth time, the fifth time, and it's not as easy for them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，第四次、第五次，这对他们来说并不容易。

sentences.en: I thought, well, those kids are destined to be at the very bottom of the class.
sentences.zh: 我心想，这些孩子注定要在班里垫底。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that that wasn't at all true.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这种想法完全错误。

sentences.en: There were some quick learners who did well, and there were some kids for whom math was more difficult, who did poorly.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些学得快的孩子表现很好，也有一些觉得数学更难的孩子表现很差。

sentences.en: But there were more exceptions than I could have ever imagined.
sentences.zh: 但出现的例外情况比我预想的要多得多。

sentences.en: By the end of the year, when I looked at the final grades, and I thought, wow, you know, this girl, this boy,
sentences.zh: 到年底，当我查看期末成绩时，我心想，哇，你知道，这个女孩，这个男孩，

sentences.en: wow, they did a lot better than I thought they were going to do.
sentences.zh: 哇，他们表现得比我预想的要好得多。

sentences.en: And gosh, you know, these other kids who I thought were going to do fantastically well,
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道，那些我以为会表现得非常出色的孩子，

sentences.en: hmm, they didn't do well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们表现得并不好。

sentences.en: So I think that the thing that was revelatory to me was not that effort matters.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，让我感到醍醐灌顶的并不是“努力很重要”这一点。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that effort matters.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道努力很重要。

sentences.en: What was revelatory to me was how much it mattered.
sentences.zh: 让我感到醍醐灌顶的是，努力竟然如此重要。

sentences.en: Since her days as a schoolteacher, Angela has made an academic career of studying this one character trait.
sentences.zh: 自当老师以来，安吉拉将研究这一性格特质作为了自己的学术生涯。

sentences.en: And that is grit, the combination of passion and perseverance for very long-term goals.
sentences.zh: 那就是坚毅，即对长期目标的激情与坚持。

sentences.en: I found it interesting that Angela focused on the subject because in our society,
sentences.zh: 我觉得安吉拉专注于这个课题很有意思，因为在我们的社会中，

sentences.en: it seems that there's this image of the genius who doesn't really have to work very hard.
sentences.zh: 似乎存在一种天才的形象，即他们并不需要付出太多的努力。

sentences.en: I think the popular imagination has it right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为大众的想象既有对的地方，也有错的地方。

sentences.en: I think if you have the intuition that somebody like Einstein or Picasso,
sentences.zh: 如果你直觉认为像爱因斯坦或毕加索这样的人，

sentences.en: that they, you know, had a certain ability or a sensitivity, a sensibility, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有某种能力或敏锐度、感知力，我认为这是对的。

sentences.en: I don't think Einstein was just like another guy on the street and nor was Picasso.
sentences.zh: 我不认为爱因斯坦只是街上的普通人，毕加索也不是。

sentences.en: So I think having some intuition that there is an ability part of the achievement, talent is one way to name that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，直觉上认为成就中包含能力成分是正确的，天赋就是一种命名方式。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是对的。

sentences.en: I don't want to be the one to say that Einstein wasn't talented nor is Picasso.
sentences.zh: 我不想成为那个说爱因斯坦或毕加索没有天赋的人。

sentences.en: But that other thing that they did, which was to work furiously hard with a kind of obsessive love for a very narrow, in the end, you know,
sentences.zh: 但他们做的另一件事，就是以一种痴迷的热爱，疯狂地投入到极其狭窄的领域中，你知道，

sentences.en: domain in which they decided to go forward and not kind of diversify and do six things, 12 things.
sentences.zh: 他们决定深耕的领域，而不是分散精力去做六件事、十二件事。

sentences.en: I think that's also important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点同样重要。

sentences.en: And that second thing, you know, really being able to focus for a long time on something that you love and it's so important to you that it kind of wakes you up every day
sentences.zh: 而第二点，你知道，真正能够长时间专注于你所热爱的事物，并且它对你如此重要，以至于它每天都能唤醒你，

sentences.en: and is the last thing you think about before you go to bed.
sentences.zh: 而且是你睡前最后想的事情。

sentences.en: I think that's also true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是事实。

sentences.en: So the popular intuition isn't wildly off.
sentences.zh: 所以大众的直觉并没有完全偏离。

sentences.en: It's importantly incomplete.
sentences.zh: 只是它在重要性上是不完整的。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting things Angela told me is that there might be a psychological reason why we want to think of genius as being effortless.
sentences.zh: 安吉拉告诉我最有趣的事情之一是，我们之所以想把天才看作是毫不费力的，可能是有心理原因的。

sentences.en: There is a fluency and an ease with which true mastery and expertise always expresses itself, whether it be in writing, whether it be in a mathematical proof,
sentences.zh: 真正的精通和专业知识在展现时，总是带着一种流畅与从容，无论是在写作中，还是在数学证明中，

sentences.en: whether it be in a dance that you see on stage, really in every domain.
sentences.zh: 无论是在舞台上看到的舞蹈，实际上在任何领域都是如此。

sentences.en: But I think the question is, you know, where does that fluency and mastery come from?
sentences.zh: 但我认为问题在于，你知道，这种流畅与精通究竟从何而来？

sentences.en: And those hours and hours of laborious effort, of misfires, of poorly written drafts, of, you know, falling on your butt when you're trying to do a turn, those things are hidden.
sentences.zh: 那些数不清的艰苦努力、失败的尝试、写得糟糕的草稿，你知道，当你试图做旋转动作时摔倒在地上，这些东西都被隐藏起来了。

sentences.en: And I think there's motivation for the performer to hide that, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为表演者有动机去隐藏这些，对吧？

sentences.en: So if I showed you, Shankar, my 197 drafts of the manuscript that finally got produced, you know, what effect would that have when you then read the 198th draft?
sentences.zh: 如果我向你展示我那197份最终成稿的草稿，你知道，当你读到第198份草稿时，会有什么影响？

sentences.en: You know, Nietzsche, the German philosopher, said that when there is excellence, you know, if we know whence it became, right,
sentences.zh: 你知道，德国哲学家尼采说过，当卓越出现时，如果我们知道它从何而来，对吧，

sentences.en: if we know its messy origins, we immediately grow cool, Nietzsche said.
sentences.zh: 如果我们知道它杂乱的起源，我们立刻就会变得冷淡，尼采说。

sentences.en: We want it to come out of the ground as if by magic.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它像魔法一样从地里冒出来。

sentences.en: And I think the motivation from the performer has a parallel motivation from the audience.
sentences.zh: 我认为表演者的这种动机与观众的动机是平行的。

sentences.en: You know, why does the audience want to hide the effort?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么观众想要隐藏努力的过程？

sentences.en: Here, Nietzsche had a very observant insight, which is to say that if we believe that what you can do is because you have a gift that I don't do,
sentences.zh: 在这里，尼采有一个非常敏锐的洞察，即如果我们相信你所能做到的仅仅是因为你有我没有的天赋，

sentences.en: here, Nietzsche says, I do not have to compete.
sentences.zh: 在这里，尼采说，我就不必去竞争了。

sentences.en: Here, the audience can relax, shoulders back, sit into your chair, and just marvel at something where you don't even have any obligation to try yourself to match the performance.
sentences.zh: 在这里，观众可以放松下来，向后靠在椅背上，惊叹于某件事，而你甚至没有任何义务去尝试达到同样的表演水平。

sentences.en: That is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: So, in other words, when you present genius as being effortless, at some level, it's more pleasurable to the audience than if you present genius as being the product of very,
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，当你把天才呈现为毫不费力时，在某种程度上，这比你把天才呈现为非常艰苦工作的产物，

sentences.en: very hard work.
sentences.zh: 对观众来说更令人愉悦。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是事实。

sentences.en: I mean, one of my favorite thinkers on this topic is a sociologist at Hamilton named Dan Chambliss.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个话题上我最喜欢的思想家之一是汉密尔顿学院的一位社会学家，名叫丹·钱布利斯（Dan Chambliss）。

sentences.en: Now, Dan is, you know, well into adulthood now, but he was a competitive swimmer all throughout high school, into college, and even in his first couple of years, I think,
sentences.zh: 丹现在已经步入成年，但他整个高中、大学期间都是一名竞技游泳运动员，甚至在他担任助理教授的头几年，我想，

sentences.en: of being an assistant professor, was still coaching.
sentences.zh: 他还在执教。

sentences.en: And he spent six years with swimmers at all levels of, you know, from the local club swim team to, you know, Olympic hopefuls.
sentences.zh: 他花了六年时间观察各级游泳运动员，从当地俱乐部游泳队到奥运会预备选手。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things that he, you know, observed that surprised him was that how excellence is really the confluence of many, many, many small acts, each of them doable,
sentences.zh: 我认为他观察到的令他惊讶的事情之一是，卓越实际上是许多许多微小行为的汇聚，每一个都是可行的，

sentences.en: each of them able to be honed with practice.
sentences.zh: 每一个都可以通过练习来磨练。

sentences.en: When you put it all together, there is a kind of mystery to it or magic to it.
sentences.zh: 当你把这一切放在一起时，它就带有一种神秘感或魔力。

sentences.en: He titled his article on this, The Mundanity of Excellence, to suggest that really, if you ask the question, whence it became, you do get to this kind of like, oh,
sentences.zh: 他将关于此的文章命名为《卓越的平凡》（The Mundanity of Excellence），以暗示如果你问它从何而来，你确实会得到这种答案，哦，

sentences.en: 10,000 small acts, each of them very doable, none of them terribly interesting.
sentences.zh: 一万个微小的行为，每一个都非常可行，没有一个特别有趣。

sentences.en: But when I was talking to him more recently about his older work, he started to describe what it was like to watch spits, the great, you know, American swimmers.
sentences.zh: 但最近我和他谈论他早期的工作时，他开始描述观看斯皮茨（Spitz）——那位伟大的美国游泳运动员——比赛是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, when he got into the pool, I mean, it was like he was a fish.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，当他进入泳池时，我的意思是，他就像一条鱼。

sentences.en: And I could hear the awe in his voice.
sentences.zh: 我能听到他声音里的敬畏。

sentences.en: It was, you know, like describing somebody who really was superhuman.
sentences.zh: 这就像是在描述一个真正超人般的存在。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think we both then had the insight that all of us, no matter what we study and how much we know intellectually that it is effort and it is practice.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为我们俩当时都有一个洞察，即我们所有人，无论我们研究什么，无论我们在智力上多么清楚它是努力和练习的结果，

sentences.en: And, you know, there are many unglamorous hours that don't get caught on camera.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有很多不光鲜的时刻没有被镜头捕捉到。

sentences.en: We sort of have this, you know, craving for that magic and mystery.
sentences.zh: 我们内心深处对那种魔力和神秘感有一种渴望。

sentences.en: You did a study a few years ago that looked at winners of the spelling bee.
sentences.zh: 几年前你做过一项研究，调查了拼字比赛的获胜者。

sentences.en: And you discovered something about the students and young people who did very well in the spelling bee.
sentences.zh: 你发现了一些关于在拼字比赛中表现出色的学生和年轻人的事情。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: I did that study on the spelling bee finalists with a psychologist probably well-known to your listeners named Anders Ericsson.
sentences.zh: 我和一位你们听众可能很熟悉的心理学家安德斯·埃里克森（Anders Ericsson）一起对拼字比赛的决赛选手进行了那项研究。

sentences.en: So the very popular, you know, version of his work is the 10,000-hour rule of practice.
sentences.zh: 他工作的一个非常流行的版本是“一万小时练习法则”。

sentences.en: But what Anders would say, I think, in his own words is that it's the quality of practice in addition to the quantity that really matters.
sentences.zh: 但安德斯会用他自己的话说，除了数量之外，练习的质量才是真正重要的。

sentences.en: He calls the highest quality of practice deliberate practice.
sentences.zh: 他称最高质量的练习为“刻意练习”（deliberate practice）。

sentences.en: And that's what he's found experts to do in all physical and intellectual domains that he's studied.
sentences.zh: 这就是他在所研究的所有身体和智力领域中发现专家们所做的事情。

sentences.en: So Anders and I got together and we asked a question, which is, what is the kind of practice that kids who are in the National Spelling Bee Finals do?
sentences.zh: 所以安德斯和我聚在一起，问了一个问题，那就是，参加全国拼字比赛决赛的孩子们进行的是什么样的练习？

sentences.en: What kinds of things do they do?
sentences.zh: 他们做些什么样的事情？

sentences.en: And which of these kinds of practice activities is the most effective?
sentences.zh: 这些练习活动中哪一种最有效？

sentences.en: And what personality traits predict what kind of practice kids will engage in?
sentences.zh: 什么样的人格特质能预测孩子们会进行什么样的练习？

sentences.en: So what we found is that kids do three things to win the spelling bee broadly.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，孩子们为了赢得拼字比赛，大体上会做三件事。

sentences.en: They read a lot, which they love to do.
sentences.zh: 他们读很多书，这是他们喜欢做的。

sentences.en: And they rate it about as effortless and about as enjoyable as eating ice cream.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这和吃冰淇淋一样毫不费力，一样令人愉快。

sentences.en: They also get quizzed by mom or dad, you know, by a computer.
sentences.zh: 他们还会让爸爸妈妈或者电脑给他们出题测试。

sentences.en: So your mom says, uspraca.
sentences.zh: 所以你妈妈说，uspraca。

sentences.en: You say, urspraca.
sentences.zh: 你说，urspraca。

sentences.en: U-R-S-P-R-A-C-H-E.
sentences.zh: U-R-S-P-R-A-C-H-E。

sentences.en: Urspraca, which I believe is the correct spelling and is certainly the winning word for the year that we studied spellers.
sentences.zh: Urspräche，我相信这是正确的拼写，也确实是我们研究的那一年拼字比赛的获胜词。

sentences.en: And then the final thing that we categorize from, like, looking at the journals that we ask kids to sort of keep something of a diary just to, you know,
sentences.zh: 最后一件我们分类的事情是，通过查看我们要求孩子们记的日记，只是为了，你知道，

sentences.en: tell us, you know, what kinds of things they were doing and how long they were doing and how it felt.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们他们在做什么，做了多久，感觉如何。

sentences.en: And the last category would be deliberate practice, you know, usually done alone, you know, working on things that you can't do,
sentences.zh: 最后一类是刻意练习，通常是独自完成的，专注于你做不到的事情，

sentences.en: like word origins that are not familiar to you, you know, trying to re-spell words and write vertically on a page, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如你不熟悉的词源，试着重新拼写单词，在纸上垂直书写，你知道，

sentences.en: words that you've misspelled before.
sentences.zh: 你以前拼错过的单词。

sentences.en: The kind of honing in on your weaknesses that is really crucial to the kind of deliberate practice that Anders has found in other experts.
sentences.zh: 这种专注于弱点的练习，对于安德斯在其他专家身上发现的刻意练习至关重要。

sentences.en: And what we found is that the quantity of deliberate practice was far more predictive of how far you would actually get in final competition
sentences.zh: 我们发现，刻意练习的数量比其他两种练习更能预测你在最终比赛中能走多远。

sentences.en: when you compare it to the other two kinds of practice.
sentences.zh: 当你把它与另外两种练习进行比较时。

sentences.en: And the phenomenology, that's a fancy and awful jargony word for saying the feeling of practice, really differed among these three.
sentences.zh: 而且现象学——这是一个用来描述练习感受的华丽而糟糕的术语——在这三种练习中确实有所不同。

sentences.en: So if you look at deliberate practice, it's that which kids found to be the most effortful of the three kinds of practice and the least enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看刻意练习，孩子们发现它是这三种练习中最费力的，也是最不愉快的。

sentences.en: Finally, we found that of all the personality traits that we looked at, grit was the best predictor of how much deliberate practice you'd actually get done.

sentences.en: We would like to think that people who work hard are doing it partly because they just really enjoyed what they're doing

sentences.zh: 也就是我所说的这个词，我采访过的人中，没有谁会被我视为

sentences.zh: 你知道，是一位伟大的美国游泳运动员、金牌得主和世界纪录保持者，

sentences.zh: 我真的认为你可以将坚毅的起源追溯到四种心理资产，它们
